quotation: For I prophesy as the god leads.
speaker: The Pythian Priestess

quotation: Horrors to tell, horrors for my eyes to see, have sent me back from the house of Loxias, so that I have no strength and I cannot walk upright.
speaker: The Pythian Priestess

quotation: For I persuaded you to take your mother’s life.
speaker: Apollo

quotation: Lord Apollo, you know how to do no wrong; and, since you know this, learn not to be neglectful also.
speaker: Orestes

quotation: Orestes, the murderer of me, his mother, is gone!
speaker: Ghost of Clytaemestra

quotation: In a dream you are hunting your prey, and are barking like a dog that never leaves off its keenness for the work.
speaker: Ghost of Clytaemestra

quotation: The beast has escaped from our nets and is gone.
speaker: Chorus of Furies

quotation: Be gone, you goats without a herdsman! No god loves such a flock.
speaker: Apollo

quotation: Through your oracle, you directed the stranger to kill his mother.
speaker: Chorus of Furies

quotation: Here I will keep watch and await the result of my trial.
speaker: Orestes
part_of_play: Athens: pursuit, binding song, and Athena’s arrival

quotation: The smell of human blood gives me a smiling welcome.
speaker: Chorus of Furies
part_of_play: Athens: pursuit, binding song, and Athena’s arrival

quotation: This is our song over the sacrificial victim—frenzied, maddened, destroying the mind, the Furies’ hymn, a spell to bind the soul, not tuned to the lyre, withering the life of mortals.
speaker: Chorus of Furies
part_of_play: Athens: pursuit, binding song, and Athena’s arrival

quotation: We are the eternal children of Night. We are called Curses in our homes beneath the earth.
speaker: Chorus of Furies
part_of_play: Athens: pursuit, binding song, and Athena’s arrival

quotation: What do you want to say to this, stranger, in turn?
speaker: Athena
part_of_play: Athens: pursuit, binding song, and Athena’s arrival

quotation: Together with me Loxias is responsible for this deed, because he threatened me with pains, a goad for my heart, if I should fail to do this deed to those who were responsible.
speaker: Orestes
part_of_play: Athens: pursuit, binding song, and Athena’s arrival

quotation: The mother of what is called her child is not the parent, but the nurse of the newly-sown embryo.
speaker: Apollo

quotation: In the future, even as now, this court of judges will always exist for the people of Aegeus.
speaker: Athena

quotation: This man is acquitted on the charge of murder, for the numbers of the casts are equal.
speaker: Athena

quotation: For you have not been defeated; the trial resulted fairly in an equal vote, without disgrace to you; but clear testimony from Zeus was present, and he himself who spoke the oracle himself gave witness that Orestes should not suffer harm for his deed.
speaker: Athena
part_of_play: Athens: Orestes departs and Athena reconciles the Furies

quotation: Peace endures for all time between Pallas’ citizens and these new dwellers here.
speaker: Chorus of the Processional Escort
